_meta.note: Each trap has real PYQ examples. Use these in blueprint generation to inject specific trap strategies per skeleton.

traps.name: party_leader_wrong_match
traps.description: In match-the-pair, assigns a leader to the wrong political party — especially using founders vs prominent members.
traps.mechanism: Students know Rajagopalachari was prominent in Congress but forget he FOUNDED Swatantra Party. Narendra Dev is associated with Socialist movement but not the Swatantra Party.
traps.real_pyq_example: 2024: Swatantra Party — Acharya Narendra Dev (WRONG, should be C. Rajagopalachari). Socialist Party — C. Rajagopalachari (WRONG, should be Acharya Narendra Dev / Jayaprakash Narayan).
traps.how_to_generate: Match 4 parties/movements to 4 leaders. Put 2 correct and 2 crossed (leader A matched with party B and vice versa). Use leaders who overlap across ideological movements.

traps.name: buddhist_text_author_swap
traps.description: Assigns a Buddhist/Jain/Ancient text to the wrong author or tradition.
traps.mechanism: Students know text names but not the specific sect, author, or language they belong to.
traps.real_pyq_example: 2024: Works attributed to playwright Bhasa — Madhyama-vyayoga (correct). Kavyalankara (Bhamaha), Natyashastra (Bharata), Mahabhashya (Patanjali) — all real texts by different authors.
traps.how_to_generate: Pick any Sanskrit text or classical work. Give 4 real text names but only one is correctly attributed to the person in the question. Others are real texts by real but different authors.

traps.name: constituent_assembly_president_first_vs_later
traps.description: Confuses the Provisional President with the eventual President of Constituent Assembly — or confuses with Drafting Committee Chair.
traps.mechanism: Students know Dr. Rajendra Prasad was President of Constituent Assembly and B.R. Ambedkar chaired Drafting Committee. The Provisional President (Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha) is almost always unknown.
traps.real_pyq_example: 2024: 'Who was Provisional President before Rajendra Prasad?' — Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha. Common wrong answers: Rajagopalachari, Ambedkar, T.T. Krishnamachari.
traps.how_to_generate: Ask about 'first' or 'provisional' holders of roles that later became associated with more famous people. Use the famous name as a distractor.

traps.name: government_of_india_act_provision_reversal
traps.description: States a provision of GOI Act 1935 incorrectly — e.g., says defence/foreign affairs were under federal legislature when they were reserved for Governor-General.
traps.mechanism: Students know GOI 1935 had federation and residuary powers but get confused on what was 'reserved' vs 'transferred'.
traps.real_pyq_example: 2024: Statement 1 (All-India Federation with provinces and princely states) — TRUE. Statement 2 (Defence and Foreign Affairs under federal legislature) — FALSE. These were reserved subjects under Governor-General.
traps.how_to_generate: Pick any colonial legislation (GOI 1919, 1935, Rowlatt Act). State 2 provisions, one of which misassigns who controlled a key subject.

traps.name: ryotwari_zamindari_feature_swap
traps.description: Assigns a feature of Zamindari to Ryotwari or vice versa — especially regarding exemptions for bad harvest.
traps.mechanism: Students mix up the two settlement systems. Ryotwari had direct settlement with ryots, Zamindari had intermediaries.
traps.real_pyq_example: PYQ: 'Under Ryotwari Settlement, peasants were exempted from revenue payment in case of bad harvests' — this is actually a nuanced TRUE. The trap is students think only Zamindari had exemptions.
traps.how_to_generate: State a feature of one revenue settlement system and attribute it to the other. Or use a feature that sounds like it belongs to the more 'exploitative' system but actually belongs to the supposedly 'better' one.

traps.name: buddhist_monk_text_tradition_wrong
traps.description: Names an Indian Buddhist monk and asks which text they wrote — confuses Theravada/Mahayana/Sarvastivada traditions.
traps.mechanism: Students know major Buddhist texts (Prajnaparamita, Visuddhimagga) but cannot match them to specific monks and schools.
traps.real_pyq_example: 2024: Sanghabhuti — wrote commentary on Sarvastivada Vinaya. Distractors: Prajnaparamita Sutra (Mahayana), Visuddhimagga (Theravada), Lalitavistara (Mahayana biography of Buddha).
traps.how_to_generate: Name an obscure monk/scholar. Distractors = real texts from other traditions. Correct answer = the matching tradition's text.

traps.name: unesco_heritage_year_wrong
traps.description: Lists UNESCO World Heritage sites and asks which were added in a specific year — students confuse recent vs older listings.
traps.mechanism: Students know which sites ARE on the list but not the exact year of inscription.
traps.real_pyq_example: 2024: Shantiniketan and Sacred Ensembles of Hoysalas were added in 2023 (answer = 2). Rani-ki-Vav (2014) and Mahabodhi Temple (2002) are old listings used as distractors.
traps.how_to_generate: Mix 2-3 recent inscriptions with 1-2 older well-known ones. Ask 'how many were added in year X'. Answer is never 'all four'.

traps.name: exercise_military_wrong_country
traps.description: Names a bilateral military exercise and assigns it to the wrong country pair.
traps.mechanism: Students know exercise names but mix up which two countries participate, especially India-Sri Lanka vs India-Bangladesh vs India-Nepal.
traps.real_pyq_example: 2024: Exercise Mitra Shakti 2023 — Statement 1 'between India and Bangladesh' — FALSE. It is India-Sri Lanka. Commenced at Aundh, Pune (TRUE). Counter-terrorism goal (TRUE). IAF part (TRUE).
traps.how_to_generate: Name any bilateral exercise (Mitra Shakti, Shakti, Yudh Abhyas, SLINEX). State the partner country wrong. India's south Asian neighbours are interchangeable in student memory.
